claim: After Ca2+ triggering, WT SNAP25 supported the largest amount of fusion, followed by V48F, whereas D166Y Ca2+-dependent fusion was clearly reduced.
source: After Ca2+ triggering, WT SNAP25 supported the largest amount of fusion, followed by V48F, whereas D166Y Ca2+-dependent fusion was clearly reduced (Figure 8D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 8D showing the in vitro fusion data.

claim: The in vitro assay reproduces both the increased spontaneous release and the reduced Ca2+-dependent release found in neurons.
source: Thus, the in vitro assay reproduces both the increased spontaneous release and the reduced Ca2+-dependent release found in neurons, indicating that these features are present within the minimal set of fusion proteins included in this assay (i.e. the SNAREs, Syt1 and complexin).
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a conclusion from comparing in vitro and neuronal data.

claim: D166Y and V48F represent partial gain-of-function mutations that increase association to partner SNAREs.
source: D166Y and to a lesser degree V48F revealed enhanced stimulation of fusion in comparison to WT before calcium was added, regardless of the presence or absence of complexin (Figure 9B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 9B showing the in vitro fusion data.

claim: D166Y showed profoundly increased interactions with SUVs containing either syntaxin-1, or VAMP2, or Syt1/VAMP2, and the combination used in the fusion assay.
source: D166Y showed profoundly increased interactions with SUVs containing either syntaxin-1, or VAMP2, or Syt1/VAMP2, and the combination used in the fusion assay (Figure 9D; Figure 9—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 9D and supplement showing the co-flotation data.

claim: V48F displayed mildly increased binding to syntaxin-1 and Syt1/VAMP1 SUVs.
source: V48F displayed mildly increased binding to syntaxin-1 and Syt1/VAMP1 SUVs, and a tendency to increased association to VAMP2 SUVs (p = 0.0629, one-sample t-test).
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a finding from the co-flotation assay.

claim: Loss of Syt1 interaction upon mutation in the primary interface can be accompanied by a gain-of-function phenotype stimulating interactions with the other SNARE partners.
source: These data show that loss of Syt1 interaction upon mutation in the primary interface can be accompanied by a gain-of-function phenotype stimulating interactions with the other SNARE partners.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a conclusion from the co-flotation data.

claim: SNARE complexes formed with the I67N mutant displayed a lower stability, with the melting temperature reduced from 71°C to approximately 56°C.
source: In in vitro experiments, SNARE complexes formed with the I67N mutant displayed a lower stability, with the melting temperature reduced from 71°C to approximately 56°C (Figure 8A)
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 8A showing the stability data.

claim: I67N showed a strong decrease in SUV docking.
source: I67N also showed a strong decrease in SUV docking (Figure 8B, C)
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 8B, C showing the docking data.

claim: In lipid mixing assays, I67N strongly reduced both Ca2+-independent and Ca2+-dependent fusion.
source: In lipid mixing assays, I67N strongly reduced both Ca2+-independent and Ca2+-dependent fusion, whether the t-SNAREs were preassembled (Figure 8D, E) or not (Figure 9B, C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figures 8D, E and 9B, C showing the fusion data.

claim: The I67N mutation is inferior in membrane fusion.
source: Overall, these data indicate that I67N is inferior in membrane fusion.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a conclusion from the in vitro data.

claim: Lentiviruses encoding the I67N mutant expressed similar amounts as WT EGFP-SNAP25b.
source: Lentiviruses encoding the I67N mutant N-terminally fused to EGFP expressed similar amounts as WT EGFP-SNAP25b (Figure 10A–C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 10A-C showing the Western blot data.

claim: Expression of I67N in SNAP25 KO neurons resulted in reduced rescue of survival.
source: Expression in SNAP25 KO neurons resulted in reduced rescue of survival in neurons expressing I67N alone
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a finding from neuronal culture experiments.

claim: Patch-clamp measurements demonstrated strongly reduced spontaneous release frequencies in the I67N mutation.
source: Patch-clamp measurements demonstrated strongly reduced spontaneous release frequencies (Figure 10H–J) and evoked release amplitude (Figure 10K, L) with the I67N mutation
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 10 showing the electrophysiology data.

claim: Patch-clamp measurements demonstrated strongly reduced evoked release amplitude in the I67N mutation.
source: Patch-clamp measurements demonstrated strongly reduced spontaneous release frequencies (Figure 10H–J) and evoked release amplitude (Figure 10K, L) with the I67N mutation
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 10 showing the electrophysiology data.

claim: The I67N is dominant negative for both spontaneous and evoked release.
source: The I67N therefore is dominant negative for both types of release, in contrast to the incompletely dominant phenotypes of the V48F and D166Y mutants (see above).
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a conclusion from the co-expression data.

claim: Application of 0.25 M sucrose did not lead to any measurable release in I67N expressing cells.
source: Application of 0.25 M sucrose did not lead to any measurable release in I67N expressing cells, and only minimal release in cells co-expressing WT and I67N (Figure 11B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 11B showing the data.

claim: 0.5 M sucrose displayed reduced release in the I67N and WT + I67N condition.
source: Indeed, 0.5 M sucrose displayed reduced release in the I67N and WT + I67N condition (Figure 11C)
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 11C showing the data.

claim: The RRP as assessed by 0.75 M sucrose (RRP0.75) was unchanged between WT, I67N, and WT + I67N co-expressed cells.
source: Strikingly, the RRP as assessed by 0.75 M sucrose (RRP0.75) was unchanged between WT, I67N, and WT + I67N co-expressed cells (Figure 11E, G).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 11E, G showing the data.

claim: The RRP per se appears intact in the I67N when probed by sufficiently high concentrations of sucrose.
source: Therefore, the RRP per se appears intact in the I67N (when probed by sufficiently high concentrations of sucrose), but the vesicles face a higher apparent fusion barrier
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a conclusion from the sucrose data.

claim: The vesicles in I67N face a higher apparent fusion barrier.
source: but the vesicles face a higher apparent fusion barrier, which makes the RRP appear smaller if assessed by 0.5 M sucrose.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a conclusion from the sucrose data.

claim: The higher apparent fusion barrier in I67N explains the lower frequency of mEPSC.
source: The higher apparent fusion barrier explains the lower frequency of mEPSC in the I67N mutation, the lower degree of spontaneous fusion in in vitro assays, as well as the lower amount of Ca2+-dependent release in vitro and in the cell.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a conclusion from the data.

claim: Combining the I67N with the 4K mutation rescued spontaneous release to WT levels.
source: The 4K mutation increased the mEPSC release rate compared to WT (Ruiter et al., 2019), whereas in the combined I67N/4K mutation the spontaneous release rate was indistinguishable from WT (Figure 12A–C)
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 12A-C showing the data.

claim: In the I67N/4K mutation, evoked release was still strongly depressed compared to WT.
source: but in the I67N/4K mutation, evoked release was still strongly depressed compared to WT (Figure 12D, E).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 12D, E showing the data.

claim: The effect of charge per se is approximately the same in the I67N mutant as in the WT.
source: When combining the I67N with the 4K mutation, which introduces six extra positive fixed charges, we could place our data within the framework of our model for electrostatic triggering (Ruiter et al., 2019) and show that the effect of charge per se is approximately the same in the I67N mutant as in the WT.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a conclusion from the charge rescue experiments.

claim: V48F and D166Y mutations fall into the 'neomorph' category, where the mutated protein has novel or changed interactions or functions.
source: We have shown that two SNAP25 mutations (V48F and D166Y) that compromise interaction with Syt1 lead to complex phenotypes characterized by a combination of loss-of-function and gain-of-function features. Thereby, the mutations fall into the 'neomorph' category, where the mutated protein has novel or changed interactions or functions (Verhage and Sørensen, 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a classification of the mutations with a citation.

claim: The I67N substitution within the SNARE bundle is a dominant-negative mutation.
source: In contrast, the I67N substitution within the SNARE bundle is a dominant-negative mutation.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a classification of the I67N mutation.

claim: Both the V48F and the D166Y resulted in a decrease in the amplitude of the apparent energy barrier for fusion.
source: Both the V48F and the D166Y resulted in a decrease in the amplitude of the apparent energy barrier for fusion, whereas the I67N increased the amplitude of the apparent fusion barrier.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary of the findings.

claim: The I67N increased the amplitude of the apparent fusion barrier.
source: whereas the I67N increased the amplitude of the apparent fusion barrier.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary of the findings.
